title: Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders 2027
organization: U.S. Department of State (administered by IREX)
overview: Six-week executive-style Leadership Institute at a U.S. college or university in summer 2027 for about 550 young African leaders. Applications are open until 13 October 2026 and there is no application fee.
program_dates: Fellowship begins in the United States in June 2027 (six-week institute)
funding_details: 'A program of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government'
'There is no fee to apply for the Mandela Washington Fellowship.'
The official pages read do not itemise travel, housing, meals or stipend. Confirm in the application instructions.
eligibility: Between the ages of 25 and 35 on or before the application deadline, 'although exceptional applicants ages 21-24 may be considered'
Citizen of an eligible country; the list includes the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC)
Resident of an eligible Sub-Saharan African country, permanently residing there as of 1 February 2027 and in June 2027
Not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident; eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa
Proficient in reading, writing and speaking English
Selection criteria include a proven record of accomplishment in business, trade, emerging technologies, governance and/or security, and a commitment to return to Sub-Saharan Africa
nationality_requirements: Democratic Republic of the Congo is on the list of eligible countries
age_requirement: 25 to 35 at the deadline; exceptional applicants aged 21 to 24 may be considered
documents_required: Semi-finalists: international passport if available, or other government-issued photo ID, at the Embassy interview
application_process: Apply online before 13 October 2026
November 2026 to January 2027: semi-finalists interviewed in person by the U.S. Embassy
February or March 2027: applicants notified
March to May 2027: visa processing and mandatory pre-departure orientation
June 2027: fellowship begins
eligibility_reason: DRC citizens living in the DRC can apply and English is at professional level. An applicant under 30 falls within the 21 to 35 range, although below 25 only exceptional applicants are considered. Selection then turns on a proven record of accomplishment.
potential_issues: Deadline is 13 October 2026
The track record expected (business, trade, technology, governance or security) is thin on the recorded profile
Nationals of countries under a full or partial U.S. entry or visa suspension can apply, but finalists are selected case by case: check travel.state.gov for the DRC's current status
What the fellowship pays for is not itemised on the pages read
benefits: Six-week institute at a U.S. university
Network of African and American leaders
Possible six-week Professional Development Experience afterwards
relevance_reason: The business and governance focus matches the degree and the Ministry internship. The weak point is the leadership record, which the application essays would have to carry.

visa.support: J-1 visa; processing takes place March to May 2027 for finalists.

action: Decide this week. If you can describe concrete results from the vaccination monitoring, the Ministry internship or community work, draft the essays and apply before 13 October.

program_dates: Cohort-based; dates not on the page read
deadline_text: Cohort dates and deadlines are shown in the application portal, not on the public page read.
funding_details: The public page read does not say which costs are covered for residential phases.
eligibility: 18 to 35 years of age at the time of application
Citizen and resident of one of 14 countries, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo
Not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
Eligible to receive any necessary visa to Kenya
Merit-based open competition with interviews for semi-finalists
nationality_requirements: Burundi, Central African Republic, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda
age_requirement: 18 to 35 at the time of application
application_process: Create an account in the RLC application portal
Selection panel review, then interview of semi-finalists
eligibility_reason: The centre serves citizens and residents of the DRC aged 18 to 35, which the profile meets.
potential_issues: Next cohort dates not visible without a portal account
Cost coverage for the residential phase not stated
Programme language is English
relevance_reason: One of the few leadership programmes that lists the DRC explicitly and has no work-experience bar.

visa.support: Applicants must be eligible for any visa Kenya requires.

action: Create a portal account to see the next cohort's dates and what is paid for.

title: Obama Foundation Leaders programme
overview: Annual leadership programme for emerging leaders from Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe and the United States. Applications open each November for the following year.
deadline_text: 'Applicants from Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe, and the United States may apply in November of the preceding year to join the program.' Exact dates not announced.
expected_next_cycle: Applications expected to open in November 2026 for the next cohort; exact dates not announced.
funding_details: Not stated on the page read.
eligibility: From Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe or the United States
Between the ages of 24 and 45 during the programme
application_process: Sign up for Obama Foundation emails to be told when applications open
eligibility_reason: African applicants are eligible, but participants must be at least 24 during the programme, so the exact age decides. The programme also looks for people already leading community work.
potential_issues: Minimum age of 24
Format (online or in person) and costs not stated on the page read
Expects an established record of community leadership
relevance_reason: Valuable network, but selection rewards a visible leadership record that the profile does not yet document.
action: Sign up for the Foundation's emails and look again in November 2026.
notes: Format was not stated on the page read; the location fields are left unknown rather than assumed.

title: Community Solutions Program
organization: IREX, sponsored by the U.S. Department of State
overview: Four-month professional fellowship in the United States for community leaders. The official page still describes the 2025 cycle and no later call has been published.
program_dates: The page read still says 'four months from August to December 2025'
deadline_text: No current call. The official page still refers to travel 'from August to December 2025'.
funding_details: The programme covers the cost of most expenses associated with: J-1 visa support; round-trip travel from the participant's home city to the U.S.; a monthly allowance for housing, meals and other living expenses; accident and sickness health coverage
eligibility: Citizen of an eligible country; the Africa list includes the Democratic Republic of Congo
At least two years of experience working on community development, as a full-time or part-time employee or volunteer
Semi-finalists must pass or submit a recent TOEFL or IELTS score
Able to travel to the U.S. unaccompanied for four months
Eligible for a U.S. J-1 visa
nationality_requirements: Africa: Botswana, Cameroon, Democratic Republic of Congo, Ghana, Guinea, Kenya, Liberia, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe
age_requirement: Secondary sources gave 26 to 39 for the 2025 cycle; not on the page read
experience_requirement: At least two years of community development work (paid or volunteer)
language_requirement: English; TOEFL or IELTS for semi-finalists
application_process: Download the application instructions from the IREX page when a cycle opens
Questions: apply.csp@irex.org
eligibility_reason: The programme requires at least two years of community development experience. The profile records under one year of short assignments.
potential_issues: No open cycle: the page has not been updated since the 2025 cycle
Two-year experience requirement
benefits: Travel, monthly allowance and health coverage
relevance_reason: Lists the DRC and funds everything, so worth knowing about, but out of reach until two years of community work are documented.
action: No action now. Volunteer work started today counts toward the two-year requirement for a later cycle.

title: French-African Foundation Young Leaders programme
overview: Annual programme bringing together young leaders from Africa and France. Applicants must be between 28 and 40.
deadline_text: No call dates on the page read. The application is made on the Foundation's website.
funding_details: Not stated on the page read.
eligibility: Age: between 28 and 40
Nationality of a country of the African continent, or French nationality
Selection by an independent jury on excellence, commitment and potential
application_process: Apply on the Foundation's website when the yearly call opens
eligibility_reason: Nationality fits, but the minimum age is 28. An applicant under 30 qualifies only if aged 28 or 29.
potential_issues: Minimum age of 28
Past cohorts average 34 years old, so candidates are usually established professionals
Dates and costs not stated
benefits: High-level network between Africa and France
relevance_reason: A strong francophone network, but aimed at people several years into their career.
action: Keep for later: revisit once you are 28 and have a few years of professional results.

title: Aspire Leaders Program (2026 Cohort 4)
overview: Free six-week online leadership programme for first-generation or limited-income university students and graduates aged 18 to 29. Cohort 4 runs from 21 October to 30 November 2026.
deadline_text: Applications for Cohort 4 of the 2026 Aspire Leaders Program are OPEN! Apply here before the October 16 deadline.
funding_details: 'No application fee. No tuition. No catch.'
Free certificate of completion; an optional verifiable e-credential bundle costs USD 5
Alumni can access seed funds and mentorship
eligibility: Limited-income or first-generation university students and graduates, anywhere in the world
18 to 29 years old
application_process: Complete the online application before 16 October 2026
eligibility_reason: The age range fits a graduate under 30. The programme is reserved for first-generation or limited-income students and graduates, and the profile does not record either.
potential_issues: Deadline is 16 October 2026
Reserved for first-generation or limited-income applicants
Live sessions need a reliable internet connection
relevance_reason: Free, short and built for recent graduates; it also adds a leadership credential that later applications (for example the Mandela Washington Fellowship) look for.
action: If you are the first in your family to attend university, or come from a limited-income household, apply before 16 October 2026.
notes: Several cohorts run each year, so a later cohort is likely if this one is missed.

deadline_text: Applications are now available to youth leaders ages 17-26. Applications close November 15, 2026.
funding_details: 'The 2027 Program is provided free to accepted applicants.'
eligibility: High-potential youth aged 17 to 26
Living in a least developed or developing country
Demonstrated talent and passion for leadership, scholarship or innovation
Proficient in English, with access to a computer and the internet
nationality_requirements: Residents of least developed and developing countries
application_process: Apply on the Kectil site before 15 November 2026
eligibility_reason: Country and language fit. The upper age limit is 26, so 'under 30' does not settle it: the exact age decides.
potential_issues: Age limit of 26
Requires a computer and internet access for webcasts
